sections.title: A shorter, more emotional wish
sections.content: bárcsak ("if only") is a more compact, more emotional way to wish for something — no szeretném needed, just bárcsak followed directly by a verb in the conditional. It leans on the same conditional you already use, minus the "I would like it" framing: Bárcsak sikerülne! stands alone as a complete wish, closer to English "If only it would work out!" than to a full sentence with a subject and object.

sections.title: bárcsak + conditional
rows: If only my plan would succeed!
If only I had more time!
If only I could dance better!

items.english: If only my dream would come true!
If only I didn't have to work this much!

sections.content: Negate a bárcsak-wish with ne, not nem — Bárcsak ne esne az eső! ("If only it weren't raining!"), never Bárcsak nem esne. This is the same ne you already know from commands (Ne menj!) — Hungarian treats a wish as grammatically close to an unreal command.
